forces.title: Strategic shift towards critical minerals impacts precious metals investment
forces.description: Mining companies are increasingly re-evaluating their portfolios, prioritizing strategic critical minerals over traditional precious metals. This structural shift is driven by global national security imperatives and the growing demand for materials essential for electrification, renewable energy, and defense technologies. This trend implies a potential diversion of capital and operational focus away from pure-play precious metal mining projects, affecting long-term investment and supply dynamics within the Precious Metals & Gems sector.

viewpoints.title: Mining firms diversifying portfolios, reducing focus on traditional precious metals
viewpoints.description: The mining sector is undergoing a strategic rebalancing as companies increasingly diversify their portfolios beyond traditional precious metals like silver. A major Indian miner, for example, plans to expand into new critical metals such as neodymium, tungsten, and potash by 2030. This shift, highlighted by Deloitte UK, is driven by national security priorities and the escalating demand for critical minerals essential for the energy transition, potentially leading to a cautious outlook for pure-play precious metal investments.
